title: When bicam convenes for 2027 budget, advocates want to be in the room
summary: ‘Ang mga tinanggal ng Senado sa ngalan ng paglaban sa korupsiyon ay hindi dapat palihim na ibalik sa bicam sa ngalan ng kompromiso,’ says Social Watch Philippines co-convenor Maria Victoria Raquiza

blocks.text: BUDGET WATCH. Social Watch Philippines holds a press conference as the Senate conducts plenary deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget on November 26, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines – Budget watchdog Social Watch Philippines wants civil society groups to be present in person when the bicameral conference committee convenes to tackle the proposed 2027 national budget.

“Panawagan talaga natin…ay nando’n tayo mismo, on-site sa bicameral conference committee meeting para namo-monitor natin ang aktuwal na nangyayari,” Social Watch Philippines co-convenor Maria Victoria Raquiza said in a press conference on Thursday, November 26.
“Hindi ‘yong sa nangyari last year na livestreaming nga, open bicam nga, pero sa totoo lang, ang major decisions ay ginawa off-camera,” she added.

(Our appeal is for us to be allowed on-site at the bicameral conference committee meeting so we can monitor what’s actually happening. We don’t want a repeat of last year where there was livestreaming, it was supposedly an open bicam, but in reality, the major decisions were made off-camera.)
Raquiza also said advocates want to have a voice during the proceedings.

Following the Senate’s briefing with civil society organizations in October, Senator Ping Lacson invited them to join the 2027 budget bicam. He also floated the idea of keeping the meeting open even if bicam members ask for session suspensions.
Raquiza said the Senate must publicize 2027 budget amendments so that civil society groups can scrutinize these changes before the bicam meeting.

Among the changes introduced by the Senate finance committee is the realignment of P19.8 billion from government assistance programs, including the Medical Assistance Program and the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations, to augment funding for the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth).
This boosted PhilHealth’s budget from P73 billion in the House version of the general appropriations bill (GAB) to P94.2 billion in the Senate committee report.
Social Watch Philippines noted that the updated figure still falls short of the P244-billion funding requirement of the state health insurer next year.

The group added that while the budget for health promotion went up from P485 million in the House GAB to P1.55 billion in the Senate version, it is still lower than the minimum 1% of the total Department of Health budget of P273 billion, supposedly violating the Universal Health Care Act.

The Senate also introduced a P97-billion reduction in the allocation for over 3,400 “non-compliant” projects of the Department of Public Works and Highways. The funding would be realigned to foreign-assisted infrastructure projects.
“Ang mga tinanggal ng Senado sa ngalan ng paglaban sa korupsiyon ay hindi dapat palihim na ibalik sa bicam sa ngalan ng kompromiso,” Raquiza said.
(What the Senate removed in the name of fighting corruption must not be stealthily returned during the bicam in the name of compromise.) – Rappler.com
